alabama.agency_name: Alabama Medicaid Agency and Alabama Department of Human Resources
alabama.apply_note: MyDHR is the Alabama Department of Human Resources online portal, where you can apply for SNAP (Food Assistance) and check your case; Medicaid applications go through the Alabama Medicaid Agency separately.
alabama.medicaid_note: Alabama has not expanded Medicaid, so adults qualify only if they fit a specific group — children, pregnant women, very low-income parents (about 18% of the poverty level), or people who are aged, blind, or disabled — and most childless adults do not qualify at any income.
alabama.state_note: SNAP applications are filed with the DHR office in your county, and five counties (Dallas, Elmore, Montgomery, Talladega, and Tuscaloosa) now use a newer portal called ACES instead of MyDHR.

alaska.agency_name: Alaska Department of Health, Division of Public Assistance
alaska.apply_note: Alaska Connect is the Division of Public Assistance online portal, where one application covers Medicaid, SNAP, cash assistance (ATAP), and other programs.
alaska.medicaid_note: Alaska expanded Medicaid, so most adults with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level can qualify, including adults without children; children and pregnant women are covered through Denali KidCare.
alaska.state_note: Alaska uses its own higher poverty guidelines, so income limits are higher than in most states, and people in remote villages can apply through a local DPA office or a village fee agent.

arizona.agency_name: Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System (AHCCCS) and Arizona Department of Economic Security
arizona.apply_note: Health-e-Arizona Plus (HEAplus) is the state's combined online portal for AHCCCS Medicaid, Nutrition Assistance (SNAP), and Cash Assistance, available in English and Spanish.
arizona.medicaid_note: Arizona expanded Medicaid (called AHCCCS), so most adults with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level can qualify, including adults without children.
arizona.state_note: A federal law enacted in 2025 adds a work requirement for Medicaid expansion adults starting January 1, 2027, so watch for notices from AHCCCS about reporting work or other activities.

arkansas.apply_note: Access Arkansas is the Department of Human Services online portal, where one application covers Medicaid and ARHOME, SNAP, and cash assistance (TEA).
arkansas.medicaid_note: Arkansas expanded Medicaid through ARHOME, so adults ages 19 to 64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level can qualify, including adults without children, and most get coverage through a private health plan paid for by Medicaid.
arkansas.state_note: ARHOME is adding community engagement (work) rules that take full effect January 1, 2027, so expansion enrollees should watch for notices from DHS about reporting work, school, or volunteering.

california.agency_name: California Department of Health Care Services and California Department of Social Services
california.apply_note: BenefitsCal is California's statewide online portal for applying for Medi-Cal, CalFresh (SNAP), CalWORKs cash aid, and General Assistance, with your county office deciding the case.
california.medicaid_note: California expanded Medi-Cal, so most adults with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level can qualify, including adults without children.
california.state_note: Applications are handled by your county, not the state, and if you have little or no money for food, ask the county to screen you for expedited CalFresh, which can arrive within three days.

colorado.agency_name: Colorado Department of Health Care Policy and Financing and Colorado Department of Human Services
colorado.apply_note: Colorado PEAK is the state's online portal for applying for Health First Colorado (Medicaid), SNAP food assistance, cash assistance, and other benefits.
colorado.medicaid_note: Colorado expanded Medicaid (called Health First Colorado), so most adults with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level can qualify, including adults without children.
colorado.state_note: Applications are processed by your county human services office, and if you are in urgent need, SNAP can be approved as fast as seven days after you apply.

connecticut.apply_note: ConneCT is the Department of Social Services online portal, where one application covers HUSKY Health (Medicaid), SNAP food assistance, and cash assistance.
connecticut.medicaid_note: Connecticut expanded Medicaid through HUSKY Health, so most adults with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level can qualify, including adults without children (covered under HUSKY D).
connecticut.state_note: HUSKY A covers children, parents, and pregnant people, HUSKY C covers older adults and people with disabilities, and HUSKY D covers other low-income adults, and households with almost no money can get emergency SNAP within seven days.

delaware.agency_name: Delaware Department of Health and Social Services
delaware.apply_note: Delaware ASSIST is the Department of Health and Social Services online portal, where one application covers Medicaid, SNAP (called the Food Supplement Program), cash assistance, child care, and energy help.
delaware.medicaid_note: Delaware expanded Medicaid, so most adults ages 19 to 64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level can qualify, including adults without children.
delaware.state_note: Delaware's SNAP income test is more generous than the federal minimum — most households qualify with gross income up to 200% of the poverty level — and households with little or no income can get emergency food benefits within seven days.

florida.agency_name: Florida Department of Children and Families and Agency for Health Care Administration
florida.apply_note: MyACCESS is the Florida Department of Children and Families online portal (formerly ACCESS Florida) for applying for SNAP, Medicaid, and Temporary Cash Assistance.
florida.medicaid_note: Florida has not expanded Medicaid, so adults qualify only in narrow groups — mainly parents of minor children at very low income, pregnant women, and people who are aged, blind, or disabled — and most childless adults do not qualify at any income.
florida.state_note: Florida uses a broader SNAP income test than the federal minimum (gross income up to 200% of the poverty level), and a SNAP-only application can be started on MyACCESS without creating an account.

georgia.agency_name: Georgia Department of Human Services, Division of Family and Children Services, and Georgia Department of Community Health
georgia.apply_note: Georgia Gateway is the state's online portal for applying for Medicaid and PeachCare for Kids, SNAP, TANF cash assistance, child care, and WIC.
georgia.medicaid_note: Georgia has not fully expanded Medicaid, so adults qualify only in narrow groups — mainly very low-income parents (about 35% of the poverty level), pregnant women, and people who are aged, blind, or disabled — and most childless adults do not qualify.
georgia.state_note: Georgia's separate Georgia Pathways to Coverage program covers some adults ages 19 to 64 with income up to 100% of the poverty level, but only if they complete 80 hours a month of work, school, volunteering, or other qualifying activities and report it.

hawaii.medicaid_note: Hawaii expanded Medicaid in 2014, so adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of Hawaii's higher federal poverty level can qualify for Med-QUEST, along with children, pregnant women, seniors, and people with disabilities at higher limits.
hawaii.apply_note: MyBenefits Hawaii is the state's online portal for applying for Med-QUEST (Medicaid) and SNAP, and for checking an application and uploading documents.
hawaii.state_note: Hawaii uses its own higher federal poverty guidelines, so income limits and SNAP benefit amounts are higher than on the mainland, and Med-QUEST members pick one of five QUEST Integration health plans.

idaho.medicaid_note: Idaho expanded Medicaid in 2020, so adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level can qualify whether or not they have children.
idaho.apply_note: Idalink is Idaho's online benefits portal for applying for Medicaid, food assistance (SNAP), cash assistance, and child care assistance, and for renewals and reporting changes.
idaho.agency_name: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
idaho.state_note: Starting January 1, 2027, some adults covered through Medicaid expansion must meet new work or community-engagement requirements to keep coverage.

illinois.medicaid_note: Illinois expanded Medicaid in 2014, so adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level can qualify whether or not they have children.
illinois.apply_note: ABE (Application for Benefits Eligibility) is Illinois's official portal for applying for Medicaid, SNAP, and cash assistance, and for managing a case online.
illinois.agency_name: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (Medicaid) and Illinois Department of Human Services (SNAP)
illinois.state_note: Starting January 2027, expansion adults face a federal work requirement and move to six-month renewals, so keep your ABE contact information current and respond quickly to notices.

indiana.medicaid_note: Indiana expanded Medicaid in 2015 through the Healthy Indiana Plan (HIP), so adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level can qualify.
indiana.apply_note: The FSSA Benefits Portal is Indiana's online portal for applying for Medicaid (including HIP), SNAP (Food Assistance), TANF, and child care assistance.
indiana.agency_name: Indiana Family and Social Services Administration
indiana.state_note: Beginning January 1, 2027, some Healthy Indiana Plan (HIP) members ages 19-64 must meet work, volunteer, training, or education requirements to keep their coverage.

iowa.medicaid_note: Iowa expanded Medicaid in 2014 through the Iowa Health and Wellness Plan, so adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level can qualify.
iowa.apply_note: Iowa's HHS Self-Service Portal is the state's online portal for applying for Medicaid, SNAP (Food Assistance), and FIP cash assistance in one application.
iowa.agency_name: Iowa Department of Health and Human Services
iowa.state_note: Starting December 1, 2026, some Iowa Health and Wellness Plan members ages 19-64 must report monthly work, school, or volunteer activity to stay covered, with many exemptions.

kansas.medicaid_note: Kansas has not expanded Medicaid, so it covers only children, pregnant women, very low-income parents (up to 38% of the poverty level), seniors, and people with disabilities, and most childless adults cannot qualify.
kansas.apply_note: ApplyForKanCare is the KanCare Medical Consumer Self-Service Portal for applying for Medicaid online; SNAP (Food Assistance) is applied for separately through the Kansas Department for Children and Families at dcfapp.kees.ks.gov.
kansas.agency_name: Kansas Department of Health and Environment (KanCare/Medicaid) and Kansas Department for Children and Families (SNAP)
kansas.state_note: If you have little or no income and need food help fast, tell your local DCF Service Center, since expedited SNAP can be decided within 7 days.

kentucky.medicaid_note: Kentucky expanded Medicaid in 2014, so adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level can qualify whether or not they have children.
kentucky.apply_note: kynect benefits is Kentucky's online portal for applying for Medicaid, KCHIP, SNAP, KTAP cash assistance, and child care assistance.
kentucky.agency_name: Kentucky Cabinet for Health and Family Services
kentucky.legal_aid_name: Kentucky Justice Online (partnership of Kentucky's four legal aid programs)
kentucky.state_note: Applications are also taken in person at a Department for Community Based Services (DCBS) office in all 120 counties.

louisiana.medicaid_note: Louisiana expanded Medicaid in 2016, so adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level can qualify whether or not they have children.
louisiana.apply_note: MyMedicaid is Louisiana's Medicaid Self-Service Portal for applying for Medicaid online; SNAP is applied for separately through the LA CAFE portal run by the Department of Children and Family Services.
louisiana.agency_name: Louisiana Department of Health (Medicaid) and Louisiana Department of Children and Family Services (SNAP)
louisiana.state_note: After approval you choose one of the Healthy Louisiana managed-care plans, and starting in December 2026 expansion adults renew every 6 months instead of yearly.

maine.medicaid_note: Maine expanded Medicaid in 2019, so adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level can qualify for MaineCare whether or not they have children.
maine.apply_note: My Maine Connection is Maine's online portal for applying for MaineCare (Medicaid), SNAP (Food Supplement), and TANF cash assistance.
maine.agency_name: Maine Department of Health and Human Services
maine.state_note: SNAP and TANF applications require an interview before eligibility is decided, and MaineCare decisions come within 45 days.

maryland.medicaid_note: Maryland expanded Medicaid in 2014, so adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level can qualify whether or not they have children.
maryland.apply_note: Maryland Benefits (formerly myMDTHINK) is Maryland's online benefits platform, and its One Application covers Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, WIC, and energy assistance in a single application.
maryland.agency_name: Maryland Department of Health (Medicaid) and Maryland Department of Human Services (SNAP)
maryland.state_note: Maryland launched the Maryland Benefits One Application in July 2025, a single mobile-friendly application for Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, WIC, and energy assistance.

massachusetts.medicaid_note: Massachusetts expanded Medicaid, so most adults under 65 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify for MassHealth.
massachusetts.apply_note: The Massachusetts Health Connector is where you apply online for MassHealth, and the same application can include SNAP by checking a box (SNAP itself is also applied for at DTAConnect.com).
massachusetts.agency_name: Massachusetts Executive Office of Health and Human Services (MassHealth for Medicaid; Department of Transitional Assistance for SNAP)
massachusetts.state_note: One MassHealth application can cover health coverage and SNAP at the same time — check the SNAP box on the form and it is sent to the Department of Transitional Assistance automatically.

michigan.medicaid_note: Michigan expanded Medicaid through the Healthy Michigan Plan, covering adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level.
michigan.apply_note: MI Bridges is Michigan's online benefits portal, where one application covers Medicaid (Healthy Michigan Plan), SNAP food assistance, cash assistance, and child care.
michigan.agency_name: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (MDHHS)
michigan.state_note: Expedited food assistance can be approved within 7 days for households with very little money, while regular food assistance decisions take up to 30 days.

minnesota.medicaid_note: Minnesota expanded Medicaid, so adults under 65 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify for Medical Assistance, the state's name for Medicaid.
minnesota.apply_note: MNbenefits is Minnesota's online portal for SNAP, cash assistance, and emergency help, while health coverage (Medical Assistance and MinnesotaCare) is applied for through MNsure.
minnesota.state_note: Minnesota splits the application in two: use MNbenefits for food and cash help and MNsure.org for health coverage, and expect a phone interview with your county after applying for SNAP.

mississippi.medicaid_note: Mississippi has not expanded Medicaid, so coverage is mainly for children, pregnant people, parents with very low incomes, and people 65 or older or with a disability, and most childless adults do not qualify no matter how low their income is.
mississippi.apply_note: Access Mississippi is the state's online portal for applying for Medicaid, SNAP, and other benefits run by the Division of Medicaid and the Department of Human Services.
mississippi.agency_name: Mississippi Division of Medicaid and Mississippi Department of Human Services (MDHS)
mississippi.state_note: Parents qualify only at very low incomes (about 24% of the poverty level), but pregnancy coverage now lasts 12 months after the birth.

missouri.medicaid_note: Missouri expanded Medicaid in 2021, so adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify for MO HealthNet, the state's name for Medicaid.
missouri.apply_note: myDSS is Missouri's online portal for applying for MO HealthNet (Medicaid), SNAP, temporary cash assistance, and child care help.
missouri.agency_name: Missouri Department of Social Services (Family Support Division and MO HealthNet Division)
missouri.state_note: Most SNAP applicants must complete an interview, usually by phone, and the state aims to decide SNAP applications within 30 days or within 7 days for urgent cases.

montana.medicaid_note: Montana expanded Medicaid, so adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify for Montana Medicaid.
montana.apply_note: apply.mt.gov is Montana's online benefits portal, where one application covers Medicaid, SNAP, cash assistance, and Healthy Montana Kids.
montana.agency_name: Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services (DPHHS)
montana.state_note: One application at apply.mt.gov covers Medicaid, SNAP, and cash aid together, and expedited SNAP can be approved within 7 days for households with very little money.

nebraska.medicaid_note: Nebraska expanded Medicaid, so adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify.
nebraska.apply_note: iServe Nebraska is the state's online portal, where one application covers Medicaid, SNAP food assistance, energy help, child care, and other benefits.
nebraska.agency_name: Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS)
nebraska.state_note: iServe Nebraska is the newer single application that replaced the older ACCESSNebraska system, and expedited SNAP can be approved in as little as 7 days for households with little or no income.

nevada.medicaid_note: Nevada expanded Medicaid, so adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify.
nevada.apply_note: Access Nevada is the state's online portal for applying for Medicaid, SNAP, TANF cash assistance, and other benefits.
nevada.agency_name: Nevada Department of Health and Human Services, Division of Welfare and Supportive Services (DWSS)
nevada.state_note: A SNAP application with just your name, address, and signature counts as filed that day, and households with little or no money may get SNAP within 7 business days.

new hampshire.medicaid_note: New Hampshire expanded Medicaid through the Granite Advantage Health Care Program, covering adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level.
new hampshire.apply_note: NH EASY is New Hampshire's online benefits portal, where one application covers Medicaid, SNAP, cash assistance, and child care.
new hampshire.agency_name: New Hampshire Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS)
new hampshire.state_note: Starting January 1, 2027, most Granite Advantage adults will have to meet work or community-engagement rules to keep their Medicaid coverage, so check the DHHS Stay Covered page before applying.

new jersey.medicaid_note: New Jersey expanded Medicaid, so adults with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify for NJ FamilyCare, the state's combined Medicaid and children's health insurance program.
new jersey.apply_note: MyNJHelps is New Jersey's online application portal for NJ FamilyCare (Medicaid), NJ SNAP, and cash assistance, and NJHelps.org offers a quick screening tool first.
new jersey.agency_name: New Jersey Department of Human Services (Division of Medical Assistance and Health Services for NJ FamilyCare; Division of Family Development for SNAP)
new jersey.state_note: New Jersey delivers benefits through county Boards of Social Services, so your county agency handles the application, and NJ SNAP guarantees a minimum monthly benefit of $95.

new mexico.medicaid_note: New Mexico expanded Medicaid, so adults up to age 65 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify, with or without children.
new mexico.apply_note: YES New Mexico is the state's one online portal for applying for Medicaid (Centennial Care), SNAP, cash assistance, and energy assistance.
new mexico.state_note: New Mexico's Medicaid program is called Centennial Care, and households with very little income or cash can get expedited SNAP within 7 days of applying.

new york.medicaid_note: New York expanded Medicaid, so most adults with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify, and adults just above that line may qualify for the state's low-cost Essential Plan.
new york.apply_note: myBenefits is the state's online portal for applying for SNAP, Medicaid, and cash assistance outside New York City, while Medicaid can also be applied for through NY State of Health.
new york.agency_name: New York State Department of Health (Medicaid) and Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance (SNAP)
new york.state_note: Outside New York City, apply through myBenefits, but in New York City benefits are applied for through ACCESS HRA instead.

north carolina.medicaid_note: North Carolina expanded Medicaid on December 1, 2023, so adults ages 19 to 64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level now qualify.
north carolina.apply_note: ePASS is North Carolina's online portal for applying for Medicaid (called Medical Assistance on the application), Food and Nutrition Services (SNAP), energy assistance, and Work First cash assistance.
north carolina.agency_name: North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services
north carolina.state_note: Applications are decided by your county Department of Social Services, and you need an NCID account to apply on ePASS.

north dakota.medicaid_note: North Dakota expanded Medicaid, so adults ages 19 to 64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify.
north dakota.apply_note: The Self-Service Portal at applyforhelp.nd.gov is where North Dakotans apply online for Medicaid, SNAP, child care assistance, and Temporary Assistance for Needy Families.
north dakota.agency_name: North Dakota Department of Health and Human Services
north dakota.state_note: North Dakota runs benefits through one statewide Customer Support Center and local Human Service Zone offices, and free help applying for SNAP is available from Great Plains Food Bank outreach workers.

ohio.medicaid_note: Ohio expanded Medicaid in 2014, so adults with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify, including adults without children.
ohio.apply_note: Ohio Benefits is the state's self-service portal for applying for SNAP (Food Assistance), Medicaid, Ohio Works First cash assistance, and child care assistance in one application.
ohio.agency_name: Ohio Department of Job and Family Services and Ohio Department of Medicaid
ohio.state_note: Ohio's benefits are run through your county Job and Family Services office, and households in urgent need can get expedited SNAP within 7 days of applying.

oklahoma.medicaid_note: Oklahoma expanded Medicaid on July 1, 2021, after voters approved it, so adults ages 19 to 64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify for SoonerCare.
oklahoma.apply_note: OKDHSLive is Oklahoma's online portal for applying for SNAP, TANF cash assistance, energy help, and child care, while SoonerCare (Medicaid) is applied for separately at MySoonerCare.
oklahoma.agency_name: Oklahoma Health Care Authority (SoonerCare) and Oklahoma Human Services (SNAP)
oklahoma.state_note: Oklahoma uses two separate portals, so apply for food and cash help at OKDHSLive and for SoonerCare health coverage at MySoonerCare.

oregon.medicaid_note: Oregon expanded Medicaid, so adults ages 19 to 64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify for the Oregon Health Plan.
oregon.apply_note: ONE (Oregon Eligibility) is the state's one online system for applying for the Oregon Health Plan (Medicaid), SNAP, cash assistance, and child care benefits with a single application.
oregon.agency_name: Oregon Department of Human Services and Oregon Health Authority
oregon.state_note: Through Healthier Oregon, people who meet the income rules can get full Oregon Health Plan coverage regardless of immigration status.

pennsylvania.medicaid_note: Pennsylvania expanded Medicaid in 2015, so adults with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify for Medical Assistance.
pennsylvania.apply_note: COMPASS is Pennsylvania's single online portal for applying for Medical Assistance (Medicaid), SNAP, cash assistance, LIHEAP, and child care help.
pennsylvania.state_note: Pennsylvania calls Medicaid Medical Assistance, and households in urgent need can get expedited SNAP within 7 days of applying.

rhode island.medicaid_note: Rhode Island expanded Medicaid in 2014, so adults ages 19 to 64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify.
rhode island.apply_note: HealthyRhode is Rhode Island's one online portal for applying for Medicaid, SNAP, RI Works cash assistance, and child care help, shared with HealthSource RI.
rhode island.agency_name: Rhode Island Department of Human Services and Executive Office of Health and Human Services
rhode island.state_note: Rhode Island uses one HealthyRhode account for Medicaid, SNAP, RI Works, and child care, and seniors and people with disabilities can use a simplified SNAP application.

south carolina.medicaid_note: South Carolina has not expanded Medicaid, so it covers mainly children, pregnant women, parents with very low incomes, and people with disabilities, while most adults without children do not qualify.
south carolina.apply_note: Apply.scdhhs.gov is the online portal for applying for Healthy Connections Medicaid, while SNAP is applied for separately through the DSS Benefits Portal.
south carolina.agency_name: South Carolina Department of Health and Human Services (Medicaid) and Department of Social Services (SNAP)
south carolina.state_note: South Carolina has not expanded Medicaid, so adults who do not qualify should check HealthCare.gov for a subsidized private plan, and SNAP uses a separate DSS Benefits Portal from the Medicaid site.

south dakota.medicaid_note: Adults ages 19 to 64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify since expansion took effect July 1, 2023, along with children, pregnant people, seniors, and people with disabilities.
south dakota.apply_note: The DSS Economic Assistance portal (called BEES) is where you apply online for Medicaid, SNAP, and cash assistance.
south dakota.agency_name: South Dakota Department of Social Services
south dakota.state_note: Starting January 1, 2027, some adults in the expansion group must meet new community-engagement (work) rules, so check with DSS for the current requirements.

tennessee.medicaid_note: TennCare covers mainly children, pregnant women, low-income parents and caretakers, seniors, and people with disabilities, and most childless adults do not qualify at any income.
tennessee.apply_note: The One DHS Customer Portal is for SNAP, Families First cash help, and child care, while TennCare (Medicaid) is applied for through TennCare Connect at tenncareconnect.tn.gov.
tennessee.agency_name: Tennessee Department of Human Services (SNAP) and TennCare (Medicaid)
tennessee.legal_aid_name: Legal Aid Society of Middle Tennessee and the Cumberlands
tennessee.state_note: Tennessee has a DHS office in every one of its 95 counties, and after applying for SNAP online you can schedule your eligibility interview right in the One DHS portal.

texas.medicaid_note: Medicaid covers children, pregnant women, low-income parents, seniors, and people with disabilities, and most childless adults do not qualify at any income.
texas.apply_note: Your Texas Benefits is the single portal to apply for Medicaid, CHIP, SNAP, and TANF cash help.
texas.agency_name: Texas Health and Human Services Commission
texas.state_note: Texas has one of the strictest parent income limits in the country, so a parent working even part-time at minimum wage can earn too much for Medicaid yet too little for marketplace subsidies.

utah.medicaid_note: Adults ages 19 to 64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify under full expansion, which took effect January 1, 2020, along with children, pregnant women, seniors, and people with disabilities.
utah.apply_note: myCase is the Department of Workforce Services portal where you apply for Medicaid, SNAP, cash assistance, and child care in one place.
utah.agency_name: Utah Department of Workforce Services (applications and SNAP) and Utah Department of Health and Human Services (Medicaid)
utah.state_note: You can turn in an incomplete application with just your name, address, and signature to start the clock on your case, then send the rest later.

vermont.medicaid_note: Adults ages 19 to 64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify for Green Mountain Care, and Dr. Dynasaur covers children and pregnant people at much higher income limits.
vermont.apply_note: Vermont Health Connect is the one place to apply for Medicaid, Dr. Dynasaur, and marketplace plans, while SNAP (called 3SquaresVT) is applied for separately through DCF's myBenefits portal at mybenefits.vermont.gov.
vermont.agency_name: Vermont Department of Vermont Health Access (Medicaid) and Vermont Department for Children and Families (SNAP)
vermont.state_note: Vermont's SNAP is called 3SquaresVT and uses a separate portal from Medicaid, so most households apply in two places.

virginia.medicaid_note: Adults ages 19 to 64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify for Medicaid (called Cardinal Care) since expansion took effect January 1, 2019, along with children, pregnant people, seniors, and people with disabilities.
virginia.apply_note: CommonHelp is the single portal to apply for Medicaid, SNAP, TANF cash help, energy assistance, and child care.
virginia.agency_name: Virginia Department of Social Services (SNAP) and Virginia Department of Medical Assistance Services (Medicaid)
virginia.state_note: Virginia's Medicaid is called Cardinal Care, and new work-reporting rules and six-month renewals for some expansion adults are scheduled to start January 1, 2027.

washington.medicaid_note: Adults ages 19 to 64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify for Apple Health (Washington's Medicaid), along with children, pregnant people, seniors, and people with disabilities.
washington.apply_note: Washington Connection is the portal for Basic Food (SNAP), cash assistance, and child care, while most adults apply for Apple Health (Medicaid) through Washington Healthplanfinder at wahealthplanfinder.org.
washington.agency_name: Washington State Department of Social and Health Services (SNAP) and Washington State Health Care Authority (Medicaid)
washington.state_note: Washington's SNAP is called Basic Food, it has no asset limit for most households, and you can use the 'See if I Qualify' screening tool on Washington Connection before applying.

west virginia.medicaid_note: Adults ages 19 to 64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify, along with children, pregnant women, seniors, and people with disabilities.
west virginia.apply_note: WV PATH is the state's online portal to apply for Medicaid, SNAP, WV WORKS cash help, and energy assistance.
west virginia.agency_name: West Virginia Department of Human Services (Bureau for Medical Services runs Medicaid; Bureau for Family Assistance handles applications and SNAP)
west virginia.state_note: Households with very low income and few resources may get expedited SNAP within 7 days, and new work rules for some expansion adults start January 1, 2027.

wisconsin.medicaid_note: Wisconsin did not adopt full expansion, but BadgerCare Plus still covers adults, including childless adults, up to 100% of the poverty level under a federal waiver, while children and pregnant people qualify at higher limits.
wisconsin.apply_note: ACCESS Wisconsin is the single portal to apply for BadgerCare Plus (Medicaid), FoodShare (SNAP), W-2 cash help, and child care.
wisconsin.state_note: Wisconsin's SNAP is called FoodShare, and tax refunds, including earned income credits, do not count as income for FoodShare.

wyoming.medicaid_note: Medicaid covers children, pregnant women, parents with very low income, seniors, and people with disabilities, and most childless adults do not qualify at any income.
wyoming.apply_note: The Wyoming Eligibility System (WES) is the online portal for Medicaid and Kid Care CHIP, while SNAP has no online application and is filed by paper or in person at a local Department of Family Services office.
wyoming.agency_name: Wyoming Department of Health (Medicaid) and Wyoming Department of Family Services (SNAP)
wyoming.state_note: Wyoming is one of the few states with no online SNAP application, so start SNAP by printing the form or visiting a local DFS office, and sending just the first page with your name, address, and signature starts the application clock.
